intro: The first cash session after Tesla's results answered a different question from the one raised by its delivery record. Buyers have seen that the company can sell cars; now they have seen the price at which shareholders will accept lower margins. The day's other retail favorites provide useful controls. Netflix gained members and fell. Sirius XM gained more than 40% without reporting results. Carvana goes into options expiry with a recent refinancing announcement and a visible strike to watch. [TSD] [NFLR] [SIRI] [CVO]

plays.title: Tesla (TSLA) | Who buys the margin reset?
parts: Why Retail Is Here

A dip buyer is being offered the same factories and the same vehicle fleet at a materially lower equity price. Thursday's nearly 10% fall followed an earnings release showing record deliveries and strong revenue. The issue was what management had to give customers to produce that volume and what investors should assume for the next round. A company able to cut prices can put pressure on smaller competitors; shareholders have to fund the strategy until lower costs or additional revenue make it profitable. That can be an attractive long-term wager and a poor reason to buy a call that expires today. [TSQ] [TSD]
What Is Driving It

Companywide gross margin was 18.2% in the June quarter and operating margin was 9.6%. These measure different stages of profitability. The former looks at revenue after cost of sales; the latter also includes operating expenses. Management also warned that production could be lower in the next quarter amid factory upgrades. The combination unsettles a model that assumes simultaneous volume growth and margin recovery. A successful upgrade may strengthen future production while creating a short-term interruption large enough to matter to estimates and contracts expiring this summer. [TSQ] [TSD]
The Social Signal

Tesla was the most discussed US stock in Thursday morning's Quiver tally for WallStreetBets. On Wednesday, before the release, Interactive Brokers described Tesla as its most active stock and single-stock option class. With the shares around $298 then, the peak probability inferred from Friday-expiry options was $290–292. The date on those observations is important. They tell us traders were committed to watching the event and that the market allowed for weakness. Thursday's decline showed where sellers found buyers. We do not yet have a new daily retail cash-flow figure from those observations. [W20] [IB] [TSD]
Historical Analog

The closest comparison is Tesla's own last earnings event. IBKR listed a roughly 9.75% decline after the previous report among a sequence of large two-sided earnings moves. A familiar percentage fall can tempt buyers to assume a familiar recovery. Yet last quarter's valuation, customer incentives and market expectations were different. The better use of the precedent is to check whether the buyer has allowed for ordinary Tesla earnings volatility. A move that looks astonishing against an index may be quite ordinary against the cost of short-dated protection in this particular stock. [IB]
Smart Money View

IBKR's pre-release analysis put near-term at-the-money implied volatility around 117%. That annualized quotation is a description of priced uncertainty, not a 117% expected move in two days. It means someone who bought event premium needed a substantial move just to cover its cost. A put owner could benefit from Thursday's decline; an out-of-the-money call owner could lose heavily despite continuing to believe in Tesla's long-run business. For ordinary stockholders the distinct issue is whether recent price cuts secure demand and capacity utilization at acceptable cash returns. [IB] [TSQ]
When the Narrative Breaks

Two observable events can defeat the dip story. More incentives without an offset in unit costs would point to persistently lower profits per vehicle. A production interruption that holds back deliveries beyond the stated upgrade period would add a volume problem to the margin problem. Conversely, better unit economics on genuine consumer demand would support the proposition that the price war is temporary. The historical $290–292 option reference belongs to the pre-earnings distribution. A return there would recover part of that repricing; it is no promise that the business problem has gone away. [TSQ] [TSD] [IB]

plays.title: Netflix (NFLX) | Buying accounts before buying earnings
parts: The Setup

Netflix fell after reporting nearly 5.9 million net paid membership additions. The immediate disappointment was how slowly that increase translated into revenue. A household converting from a shared password can begin paying late in the quarter, enter through a lower-priced plan or be added as an extra member. That is why the company can have won a customer on a Tuesday without collecting anything close to a full quarter's average revenue from them. Thursday's Quiver reading ranked Netflix fourth, making the attention measurable even as price action turned adverse. [NFL] [NFLR] [W20]
What to Watch

The fundamental test is management's expected acceleration of second-half growth. If an extra quarter of billing time lifts revenue while memberships continue to rise and advertisers pay for the viewing hours, the first reaction may have discounted the commercial opportunity too harshly. If revenue per user and advertising returns remain weak, account growth could still disappoint the equity owner. Friday's expiration adds a separate hurdle for options traders. A slow rollout can work as corporate policy while taking considerably longer than a weekly contract to justify itself. [NFL]

plays.title: Sirius XM (SIRI) | Buying scarce shares
parts: The Setup

Thursday's 42%-plus jump came on unusually high turnover, with Benzinga Pro putting short interest at about 34% of the float. Float is the portion of shares available to trade. It matters more to a squeeze than the size of the company on paper. A short seller who needs to repay a share must obtain one from the available pool. A surprisingly small increase in demand can move the price sharply if holders decline to sell. None of that establishes that individual investors supplied all the new demand or that business forecasts improved. [SIRI]
What to Watch

A lasting rerating requires evidence about subscribers, pricing and cash flow from the coming results. A squeeze only requires that borrowed shares become urgently expensive to replace. If the quote falls sharply as turnover eases, the change would be consistent with the urgent buyer having gone home. A price that holds while the company shows better subscription economics would support a different interpretation. The distinction is especially important after a one-day jump large enough to dominate the accumulated value of several quarters of modest operating improvements. [SIRI]

plays.title: Carvana (CVNA) | The $59 weekly call runs out of time
parts: The Setup

Wednesday's most active July call struck at $59, with opening purchases reported while Carvana's debt exchange drove a 40% share-price gain. Thursday morning the stock rose to second place in the WallStreetBets mentions ranking. Those observations explain why today can be volatile without any change in the debt agreement. Contracts nearing expiry have little time value left; small changes in the common share price can completely change whether a strike finishes in the money. A social mention cannot tell us which side of an option the author holds. [CVO] [W20] [CVR]
What to Watch

Judge the Friday contract by the strike plus the premium its particular buyer paid. Judge the equity over the longer term by whether the exchange, the proposed equity raise and the operating improvements proceed. One can fail while the other succeeds. A creditor willing to accept first-lien paper and accrue some interest has more security than a late buyer of the stock. As the deadline passes for the weekly options, the bondholder's calendar and the car buyer's financing decisions will be the clocks that count. [CV] [CVE]
